podcast.body: Madonna performed the title theme for the 2002 James Bond film "Die Another Day." She accepted the role, believing that Bond needed to embrace a techno sound. The song became a hit in the United States, marking the highest-charting Bond song since Duran Duran's "A View to a Kill" in 1985. "The producers wanted the theme to be a hit in the United States. So their first choice for a singer was Madonna and she accepted. She believed that Bond needed to go techno."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Madonna's famous song for a James Bond film, "Die Anode Ray," features her singing voluntarily with completely saturated Auto-Tune. This example, alongside others, illustrates that the deliberate use of Auto-Tune distortion is a recognized artistic technique employed by major artists, not exclusive to trap music. "Madonna cuando hacía la famosa canción para la película de James Bond de Die Anode Ray en el cual Madonna cantaba de manera voluntaria totalmente saturada de auto-tium."
